ordered_diagnoses: Congenital granular cell tumor of the tongue

facts.raw_span: A 20-year-old man
no significant medical history
a 1.5-cm diameter, exophytic, smooth, regular, and soft lesion on the midline of the dorsal tongue
the lesion had been present since birth and had not changed in size or character
Vital signs were within normal limits
An MRI of the tongue showed a 1.5-cm protuberant mass arising from the dorsal aspect of the tongue in the midline at the junction of the oral component and base
the lesion appeared partly fatty, likely submucosal, demonstrated mild contrast enhancement, had intact overlying mucosa, and showed no involvement of intrinsic tongue muscles
the sublingual space and major salivary glands appeared normal

concepts.preferred_label: Congenital granular cell tumor of the tongue
concepts.why: The patient's lesion is consistent with a congenital granular cell tumor, given its exophytic and smooth appearance, presence since birth, and partly fatty composition on MRI.
The midline location and partly fatty appearance of the lesion could suggest a lingual thyroid, although the absence of specific thyroid-related symptoms or findings makes this less likely.
The congenital nature and submucosal location of the lesion could be consistent with a dermoid cyst, although the partly fatty composition on MRI is not typical for this diagnosis.
The partly fatty composition of the lesion on MRI could suggest a lipoma, although the exophytic and smooth appearance is less typical for this diagnosis.
The congenital nature and benign appearance of the lesion could be consistent with a hamartoma, although the specific composition and location of the lesion are not typical for this diagnosis.

rationales.F03: The presence of a smooth, regular, and soft lesion on the midline of the dorsal tongue is consistent with several tongue lesions.
rationales.F04: The long-standing nature of the lesion suggests a congenital or benign condition.
rationales.F07: The partly fatty composition and submucosal location of the lesion are highly suggestive of a lipoma or congenital granular cell tumor.
rationales.F08: The absence of involvement of the sublingual space and major salivary glands makes lingual thyroid less likely.
